title: Online Tool for the Transfer of Work Demands: qualitative pilot study
summary:
Background: Approximately 15 years ago, the "work-related medical rehabilitation" (WMR) was introduced to promote vocational participation for patients with distinctive work-related problems due to chronic disease or disability, which are associated with an increased need for work-related interventions. WMR-services are characterized by a continuous focus on critical work demands in diagnostic and therapeutic activities. 

Since the assessment of work demands is typically based on interviews with the patients, limitations are expected if patients are unable or unwilling to accurately describe the job demands that threaten a successful reintegration into employment. The project therefore intends to involve company representatives in the assessment of work demands by implementing an online tool, which enables a low-effort, holistic, and at the same time specific transmission of work demands. A key prerequisite for the successful implementation of the online tool is its acceptance by the involved actors.

Methods: To optimally incorporate their needs, expectations, and concerns into the development of the online tool and the associated materials and media, initial interviews and focus groups will be conducted with patients, company representatives, and MBOR professionals to identify enabling conditions for their willingness to use the online tool.
conditions: Diseases of the musculoskeletal system and connective tissue

interventions.name: Five focus groups will be conducted, each comprising 5–8 rehabilitation patients, including two groups with orthopedic patients and one group each with neurological, cardiological, and psychosomatic patients from work-related rehabilitation programs. Ten interviews will be conducted with company representatives (including occupational health services, company integration management, and managerial staff) in order to identify enabling conditions for workplace stakeholders’ willingness to use the online tool.

Ten interviews will be conducted with rehabilitation professionals that are engaged in work-related diagnostics and/or workplace training in order to assess 1) the needs of MBOR stakeholders regarding the assessment of job requirements and 2) barriers and facilitators associated with rehabilitation

Arm 1: patients undergoing WMR
Arm 2: company representatives
